source_binding: Both complete catalog-storage race suites, package lint, goago, and source prose bind all ten committed files. The raw records retain concurrent module inputs separately.

external_contracts.use: Bounded current-object inventory, continuation tokens, URL encoding, and explicit truncation.
Conditional If-Match deletion, general-purpose bucket support, and retained historical versions.

limits: The original checks fail three tests because memory and S3 lack inventory and conditional-deletion capabilities. The new interface declares the contract before those checks. No prior unsafe-deletion defect is claimed.

Memory pages remain ordered and bounded through empty, boundary, and multi-page inventories. Tests cover independent returned values, invalid requests, cancellation, concurrent replacement, stale validators, and deletion.

S3 tests use the actual pinned SDK and local HTTP servers. They cover URL decoding, unchanged continuation tokens, exact conditional headers, malformed or oversized XML, incomplete metadata, duplicate keys, invalid sizes, conflicts, missing objects, denied access, unsupported operations, and pre-network rejection.
The S3 adapter limits inventory responses to 8 MiB. It rejects wildcard and multiple deletion validators and never falls back to unconditional deletion.

These are backend operations, not a complete Object RetainingStore. Inventory pages do not form a multi-page snapshot. Validators can repeat when bytes repeat, so a generation retirement protocol and publication fence remain required.

Versioned buckets can retain historical object versions after current-object deletion. Current inventory size does not measure total physical storage. The adapter does not bypass retention or delete historical versions.
Both final storage suites pass 223 test events, including parents, without failures or skips. These toolchain runs repeat the same cases and are not 446 distinct tests.

The initial lint run reported one checked integer conversion. A local SDK range check resolved it. The initial prose run reported three diagnostics. Both failed runs and passing final runs remain archived.
Live S3 service compatibility and native Windows or Linux execution remain unverified for this change. Local HTTP tests do not establish hosted-provider support.

Object generation collection, runtime protection, observation-file collection, distinct-inventory retirement, twelve mapped subcases, full verification, required review, native CI, and merge remain open. CSP5 remains unpublished until its complete contract passes.
Five concurrent tooling edits remain outside the source commit. Final task qualification must use its final committed module graph.
The final canonical prose check passes. Source snapshots separate the concurrent tooling edits from six owned documentation files. Task criteria, scope, invariants, and the goal remain unchanged.
